request: Create a design lesson comparing two glues. Students should critique the old evidence, allocate the available independent joints, specify testing and submit a blank record rather than invented results.
objective: Separate adhesive and cure-time differences and design a controlled joint-strength comparison.

sources.text: Fictional model-building log: glue P joints cured for two hours held a median of9 washers; glue Q joints cured for six hours held a median of15. Joint counts and individual failures were not retained.

Twenty-six new identical straw-joint kits are available. Each kit receives one glue and is tested once. Both glues may use either cure time; keep straw dimensions, overlap length, glue volume and room conditions equal.

Hang one identical washer every ten seconds until the joint separates; record the number held before separation, including zero, joint ID, glue, cure time and test order. Randomize order and do not reuse broken joints. No new tests exist.
